_comment: IAM policies for Fortexa/SSDT ECS deployment. Account: 459181228792, region ap-northeast-1.
_known_issue: SECURITY-RELEVANT DRIFT, checked 2026-08-13: neither 'ecsBackendTaskRole' nor 'ecsTaskRole' exist in the account anymore (confirmed via iam:GetRole — NoSuchEntity for both). The role actually attached to the backend task (fortexa-backend-task-role) does NOT use the scoped policy below — it has the AWS-managed SecretsManagerReadWrite, AmazonSESFullAccess, AmazonS3FullAccess, and CloudWatchLogsFullAccess policies attached (full read/write across ALL secrets/SES identities/S3 buckets in the account, not just this app's), plus one inline policy (FortexaGeminiSTSAccess: sts:GetCallerIdentity only). This file's scoped 'secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on ssdt/*' intent was never carried over when the role was renamed/rebuilt for the ap-northeast-1 migration. Worth deciding: tighten the live role back to least-privilege, or accept broad access and treat this file as historical/aspirational.

fortexaBackendTaskRole-liveReality._comment: What is actually attached to arn:aws:iam::459181228792:role/fortexa-backend-task-role today — AWS-managed policies, not a custom scoped document.

FortexaZapRecycleAccess._status: ATTACHED (verified 2026-08-19 via iam:GetRolePolicy). Grants ecs:ListTasks, ecs:DescribeTasks, ecs:StopTask, each conditioned on ecs:cluster = fortexa-cluster. Re-apply with: aws iam put-role-policy --role-name fortexa-backend-task-role --policy-name FortexaZapRecycleAccess --policy-document file://infrastructure/fortexa-zap-recycle-policy.json
FortexaZapRecycleAccess._known_gap: ecs:DescribeServices is NOT granted. Recycling works without it, but zapRecycler cannot read the scheduler's reason on a PLACEMENT_FAILED, so capacity failures log without the underlying ECS event text. Least-privilege addition would be ecs:DescribeServices on the zap-scan-ec2 and zap-auth-task-ec2 service ARNs only.
FortexaZapRecycleAccess._purpose: Lets the backend stop the ZAP ECS task before each scan so the container starts fresh (backend/services/zapRecycler.js). ZAP JVM never returns heap to the OS, so a long-lived task sits at ~10.6GB of 14GB indefinitely.
FortexaZapRecycleAccess._scoping_note: ecs:StopTask cannot be scoped to one service, only to a cluster. The code-side control is that zapRecycler only ever stops ARNs returned by its own ListTasks({serviceName}) call — never an ARN from a caller, request body, or DB field.

fortexaBackendTaskRole-scopedIntent._comment: Least-privilege version of what fortexa-backend-task-role needs, updated to ap-northeast-1 and the current consolidated secret. NOT currently applied — see _known_issue above.
